question: What defines the scope of healthcare waste generated in medical facilities?

options.A: Waste from diagnosis, treatment, and medical research
options.B: Expired non-prescription drugs bought outside the ward
options.C: Office supplies used exclusively by administrative staff
options.D: Only discarded food items from the hospital kitchen

explanation: Healthcare waste includes all byproducts of medical care, diagnostics, and research activities involving humans or animals. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h1)

question: Why does poor healthcare waste management pose a serious public health concern?

options.A: It attracts unwanted rodents to the administrative offices
options.B: It increases the financial cost of purchasing new hospital beds
options.C: It causes immediate structural damage to hospital buildings
options.D: It exposes workers and the community to hazardous elements

explanation: Improperly managed waste contains dangerous infectious and toxic agents that directly threaten humans and the environment. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h1)

question: What percentage of waste generated in healthcare facilities is typically hazardous?
explanation: The vast majority of hospital waste is general refuse, leaving a smaller hazardous fraction that needs special containment. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h2)

question: Surgical specimens and amputated limbs belong to which category of healthcare waste?
explanation: Recognizable body parts, tissues, and organs fall specifically under pathological waste classifications. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h2)

question: Which group of infectious agents represents the primary biological hazard in clinical settings?

options.D: Inert dust particles and mineral fibers

explanation: Biological hazards are living microorganisms or their toxins capable of causing disease in humans. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h3)

question: A nurse touches contaminated dressing material without gloves. What is the primary risk?

options.B: Systemic poisoning from heavy metal toxicity
options.C: Severe chemical burns on the epidermis

explanation: Handling infectious waste without barriers exposes the skin to viable pathogens capable of establishing an infection. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary danger associated with an accidental needle-stick injury?
explanation: Sharps penetrate the skin barrier, transferring blood and body fluids containing infectious agents directly into the victim's bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h4)

question: Why is recapping used hypodermic needles strongly discouraged in clinical practice?

options.A: It violates hospital financial accounting policies for consumables
options.B: It ruins the sharpness of the needle tip for subsequent use
options.C: It is the leading cause of accidental needle-stick injuries
options.D: It wastes valuable time during medication administration rounds

explanation: Attempting to guide a needle back into its cap frequently results in the practitioner accidentally stabbing their own hand. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h4)

question: Which hazardous metal is commonly found in traditional blood pressure apparatuses in hospitals?
explanation: Mercury is a toxic heavy metal historically used in sphygmomanometers and thermometers within clinical settings. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h5)

question: What happens when unused pharmaceutical drugs are dumped improperly into local water sources?

options.A: The water instantly purifies itself through natural sunlight exposure
options.B: Active chemical compounds contaminate the drinking water supply
options.C: Aquatic plant life grows at an unusually slow and controlled rate
options.D: The drugs crystallize and turn into harmless mineral sediment

explanation: Pharmaceutical residues leach into soil and water systems, posing long-term toxicological risks to humans and wildlife. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h5)

question: Who represents an informal group at extreme risk on municipal dumpsites in Nigeria?

options.B: Waste scavengers searching for recyclable items

explanation: Scavengers frequently comb through unsegregated hospital refuse on open dumpsites, risking direct contact with discarded sharps and infectious items. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h6)

question: Why are sanitation porters in poorly funded clinics particularly vulnerable to injury?

options.A: They spend most of their working hours administering chemotherapy drugs
options.B: They often handle heavy waste bags without proper protective gear
options.C: They are required to perform surgical procedures without supervision
options.D: They live inside hospital incinerator rooms during their shifts

explanation: Lack of personal protective equipment and inadequate training leaves support staff vulnerable to punctures and pathogen exposure. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h6)

question: What toxic compounds are released into the air during open burning of medical plastics?
explanation: Burning plastics and medical packaging at low temperatures in open air produces hazardous chemicals like dioxins and furans. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h7)

question: How can open dumping of hospital waste affect neighborhoods far from the health facility?

options.A: Groundwater levels rise significantly across the entire region
options.B: Local residents develop immediate immunity to all bacterial diseases
options.C: The waste dissolves and disappears into the upper atmosphere
options.D: Scavenging animals carry infectious waste materials into nearby areas

explanation: Animals foraging on exposed dumpsites can transport contaminated items and biological waste into surrounding residential communities. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h7)

question: Where should the initial segregation of healthcare waste take place?

options.B: At the exact point of generation

explanation: Waste must be sorted into appropriate containers immediately when it is produced by the clinician or nurse. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h8)

question: When is a sharps safety box considered ready for permanent sealing and disposal?

options.A: After sitting in the ward for one full year
options.C: As soon as the first needle is dropped inside
options.D: When it is packed to the absolute brim

explanation: Sealing a sharps box at three-quarters capacity prevents overfilling and reduces the risk of accidental punctures from protruding items. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T1#GNS122_U5_T1_h8)
